clothing.x: Clothing is a type of mechanics in coral island where the player can equip items to their respective category slot such as outfit, top, bottom, footwear, hat, glasses, or back accessory. It's purely cosmetic and doesn't have any impact to other game mechanics.
Unlike other items, article of clothing is not stackable, and beside can be stored in [[crafting|chest]], it can also be stored in [[storage|wardrobe]].

Wearing outfit generally restrict wearing another top and bottom. Similarly, once [[merfolk-blessing|Merfolk Blessing]] is obtained, tail is used in merfolk mode allow wearing another merfolk top, and restrict wearing another outfit, top, bottom, and footwear. Currently only 1 tail can be owned and equipped at any time.

masteries.x: Masteries, not to be confused with skills, are basic aspects in Coral Island that [[player|player]]s can level up. The higher the level of the mastery, the more skill points the player will have to unlock new skills.

Masteries are categorized into eight different aspects based around different aspects of the game: [[farming|Farming]], [[ranching|Ranching]], [[foraging|Foraging]], [[mining|Mining]], [[diving|Diving]], [[catching|Bug catching]], [[fishing|Fishing]], and [[combat|Combat]]. Each mastery contains six skills related to that aspect, such as improving crop prices in the Farming mastery or improving the chances of finding better resources when Mining.
Each mastery gains experience based on completing tasks relating to it and gains levels when certain amounts of experience are gained. The points are applied after the player goes to bed.

Gaining levels in any mastery can allow the player to learn new recipes and awards a skill point at every even level for the unlocking of new skills. Skills cannot be changed once they have been chosen but all skills can eventually be learned.

Experience points are required to increase the mastery level of the player. The player can earn experience points by doing various activities. Reading certain books at the [[library|Library]] will offer experience points. Some of the activities the player can do are:

r: Water or till soil, harvest [[crop|crops]], [[fruit-plant|fruit plants]], and [[fruit-tree|fruit trees]]
Pet [[farm-animal|farm animal]]s, and collect their products
Cut log, young and mature wild trees, gather land [[foraging|scavengeables]] except [[coconut-group|any coconut]]

masteries.x: When the player has gathered enough experience, the system will announce the leveling of the relevant mastery at the end of the day when the player goes to bed alongside any skill points or recipes earned from reaching that level. Skill points are awarded for every even numbered mastery level reached, while recipe unlocks can vary depending on the mastery.

Specific activities, the mastery they apply to, and the experience given are detailed on the individual mastery pages. Experience points will not be obtained once max level (level 10) for a particular mastery is reached.
Proficiency is a hidden skill that is related to the player’s ability to use tools. Developing proficiency allows the player to reduce the energy used with certain tools.
The player's proficiency goes up every time a level is gained in a mastery, but can also temporarily be improved by eating [[consumables|consumables]] that offer [[buff|bonuses]] to proficiencies.

Leveling up mastery will unlock new recipes for [[crafting|crafting]] or [[cooking|cooking]], and add to max [[energy|energy]]. Leveling all 8 masteries to 10 will obtain succès « This is Coral Island ».

Every other level of a mastery gained allows the player to unlock one skill. The player will be able to unlock up to five skills by leveling up. The last skill can be unlocked by purchasing the corresponding elixir using [[merit-points|Merit Points]].

production.x: Production is in-game mechanics to get new or refined products based on certain inputs and equipment that require certain duration. Items that are prepared through kitchen or are crafted through in-menu crafting are explained further in [[cooking|cooking]] and [[crafting|crafting]] respectively.
This wiki categorized the production into three:

i: Artisan: production which resulted in artisan products. Quality of the products depend on the inputs, except for [[tap|tap]] since there are no inputs required.
Resource: production which resulted in resources.

Producer: production which resulted in replicated item, or producing item without inputs. Quality of the products depend on the inputs, except [[solar-panel|solar panel]] since there are no inputs required.

production.x: Production can be done through equipment or building. The equipment need to be placed on the farm or in the shed, while building need to be purchased/built from [[carpenter|carpenter]] on the farm. Then, it can be interacted with certain inputs that are being brought and selected from inventory. After certain duration, the outputs can be collected. Some equipment can also be automated using [[auto-chest|auto chest]].

i: All production process will go through first in first out queue except [[dehydrator|dehydrator]], [[fish-pond|fish pond]]. and [[insect-house|insect house]] that will process all inputs simultaneously.
All production can't process different type of input at the same time except [[bee-house|bee house]] and [[dehydrator|dehydrator]].
Only [[solar-panel|solar panel]] and [[tap|tap]] don't require any inputs. [[tap|Tap]] needs to be attached to mature wild trees such as Pine, Oak, Maple, Poplar or Mahogany to produce.
Production will keep running as long as there are inputs (if applicable) and the max output slot is not filled yet.

While time to produce for most require the full time stated (e.g. 1 day = 24 hours), [[tap|tap]], [[insect-house|insect house]], and [[fish-pond|fish pond]]'s time requirement is rounded to the whole day, e.g. if they start working in the end of the day, it will still be counted as 1 whole day.

ocean-crops.x: Ocean crops are new crops added in version 1.1 of the Merfolk update.
Underwater crops are a crucial resource, as the [[merfolk-kingdom|Merfolk Kingdom]] is suffering food shortage caused by the oil roots.
How to unlock

After completing the quest « One of us », reaching [[town-rank|Ocean rank]] A and completing the ceremony, the player receives mail from [[krakatoa|King Krakatoa]], inviting them to help rebuild the Merfolk Kingdom. After visiting, they will receive the quest « Resupply Merfolk Kingdom » and unlock the [[underwater-farm|underwater farm]].
Mechanics
Obtaining seeds
Crafting

After unlocking the underwater farm, the player is given access to the [[carnivorous-plant|Carnivorous Plant]], which is an Ocean Seed Mixer. Either the ocean or land carnivorous plant can be used to create seeds.
To create an ocean crop seeds, the player provides the carnivorous plant the required land crop, ocean scavengeable and kelp. Each crafting creates 2 seeds.
Purchasing

After shipping 50 of each crop to the merfolk, the player receives access to purchase seeds directly from the [[merfolk-general-store|Merfolk General Store]]. The player can purchase [[seaweed-starter|seaweed starter]] any time.
Basics

Ocean crops have no season — they can be planted any time of the year. Like [[crop|crops]] on the land farm, ocean crops can only be planted into soil tilled by a [[hoe|hoe]]. Tilling soil consumes the player's energy. Once the soil is tilled, the player can place [[fertilizer|fertilizer]] and plant any ocean seed into that square. The tile may then be "sunned" using a [[lumina-wand|lumina wand]]; an action that also consumes the player's energy. A planted and sunned ocean seed will start growing.
When crops are ready to harvest, the player can do it manually or by using a [[scythe|scythe]], just like land crops.
Growth and regrowth times
Ocean crops can only be planted on underwater farm, and land crops can not be planted underwater.
Unlike land crops, regrow-able ocean crops have harvest limits.
Quality
The [[oracle-chamber|Oracle Chamber]] offers upgrades to the player's ocean seeds and [[seaweed|seaweed]]. Each upgrade costs a specific number of ocean crops and game money.

Upgrades purchased at the Oracle Chamber apply to all ocean seeds in the player's inventory or planted on the underwater farm and all future seed purchases with no increase in price. Once upgraded, the base quality of all ocean seed crop produce will increase.
Scarecrows
Like crows on the land farm, unprotected ocean crops might be eaten by underwater creatures unless protected by a [[scarecrow|scarecrow]].
Sunning
The player may hand light the crops using the [[lumina-wand|lumina wand]], or purchase the recipe for [[lumina-sprinkler-i|lumina sprinklers]], available at the [[oracle-chamber|Oracle Chamber]].

hangout.x: Hangout is an activity the player can do with most characters on Coral Island. To start a hangout, the player must have an empty slot chosen in their inventory so they may ask the character out. Certain weather conditions and opening hours will limit the number of hangout locations and activities. Some hangout locations are unavailable until they are unlocked by the player.
NPCs may also invite the player to hang out. The location is random and does not cost anything or count toward the weekly hangout limit.

With the 1.2 update came a new feature called Hangout Events. They are different from Heart Events, and unfortunately, cannot be seen or read again once the event is over as of the current game version (1.2). tourists.x: Tourists are visitors who come to enjoy the island's beauty and [[attractions|attractions]]. At the beginning of the game, players learn that an oil spill has significantly reduced the number of tourists in [[starlet-town|Starlet Town]], resulting in a poor [[town-rank|town rank]] score. One of the player's missions is to restore the Town Rank, and as they progress, more tourists will start visiting the town.

Tourists arrive on the 1st and 15th of each [[calendar|season]] and stay in town for the next two weeks. You can see them arriving from the beach dock on a cruise ship and heading straight to the inn at 7 A.M. They will depart from the town at 5 P.M.

Occasionally, tourists visiting Starlet Town bring or leave items in a special bin located on the dock, to the left of the welcome sign. Players can check this bin to retrieve anything the tourists have donated. As the Town Rank improves and more tourists visit the town, the items left in the box become more valuable and frequent. This makes the tourist bin a rewarding spot for players to find useful and interesting items throughout their journey.

Their schedule adjusts according to the weather. The tourists will avoid the beach during rainy weather, while the museum becomes more crowded during such conditions. During festivals, the player can also see backer tourists visiting Starlet town.

While walking around, tourists can be seen wearing different clothes based on the locations they visit. Additionally, there are special tourists known as Kickstarter Backer Tourists. These unique visitors appear occasionally during festivals and can be interacted with. The player cannot develop [[friendship|relationships]] with these tourists.

fish-trap.x: A fish trap is a [[tool|tool]] used to catch any [[fish|fish]].
The player will learn to [[crafting|craft]] fish traps as they level their [[fishing|Fishing]] mastery.
All fish traps can be placed beside any body of water, such as along a quay, bridges, seashore, or by a riverbank. Each trap occupies a 1x1 space.

Once placed, a fish trap will passively catch fish or trash. Using bait increases the chances of catching fish. The type of fish caught depends on what naturally spawns in the water where the trap is placed, and the size of fish depends on the type of trap
The traps can also be enhanced by the corresponding [[bait|baits]].

Certain waypoints may be temporarily disabled during some [[festival|festivals]]. If the waypoints are blocked, e.g. by chest, or traps or npcs, the waypoints can't be teleported to as well.

Town ranks explained
Rank F

Rank F is the starter rank. The player has access to basic vegetable crops from [[sam|Sam]] through his [[sams-general-store|General Store]]. The rancher, [[jack|Jack]], sells [[chicken|chicken]]s and [[cow|cow]]s. [[joko|Joko]] and [[dinda|Dinda]], the carpenters, can build [[coop|coop]] and [[mill|mill]] at the [[farm|farm]]. Joko's [[furniture-store|Furniture Store]] sells the Basic, Cabin Wood, and Beach furniture sets.
Rank E

By reaching Rank E, the player unlocks [[fruit-group|fruit]] seeds and more crop seeds from [[sams-general-store|Sam's General Store]]. The rancher, [[jack|Jack]], starts selling [[duck|duck]]s and [[sheep|sheep]]. [[antonio|Antonio]] opens the [[white-flamingo|White Flamingo]] clothing store. More clothing and [[furniture|furniture]] items become available. Tier one of R&D is unlocked at the lab. More [[tourists|tourists]] will visit Starlet town on a regular basis.
Rank D

By reaching Rank D, the player unlocks more and crop seeds at [[sams-general-store|Sam's General Store]]. The rancher, [[jack|Jack]], starts selling [[goat|goat]]s, and [[quail|quails]]. More new [[furniture|furniture]] and [[white-flamingo|clothing]] are also available, and tier two of R&D is unlocked at the lab. More [[tourists|tourists]] will visit Starlet town on a regular basis.
Rank C

By reaching rank C, the player earns 500 [[merit-points|Merit Points]]. They also unlock some [[fall|fall]] seeds, [[winter|winter]] seeds, and [[fruit-tree|fruit tree]]s at [[sams-general-store|Sam's General Store]]. The rancher, [[jack|Jack]], starts selling [[pig|pig]]s and [[peafowl|peafowl]]. [[joko|Joko]] and [[dinda|Dinda]] can now build level 3 [[coop|coop]] and [[barn|barn]]. More [[tourists|tourists]] will visit Starlet town on a regular basis.

After the player reaches rank B, [[jack|Jack]] starts selling [[llama|llama]] and [[luwak|luwak]]. More new [[furniture|furniture]] and [[white-flamingo|clothing]] are also available. More [[tourists|tourists]] will visit Starlet town on a regular basis.

After the player reaches rank A, new clothing becomes available, and the player earns 700 [[merit-points|Merit Points]]. [[connor|Connor]] will mail keys to the cellar on the player's farm , which gives access to more space and production machines. More [[tourists|tourists]] will visit Starlet town on a regular basis.

random-event.x: Random events can rarely occur on the [[farm|farm]] at night after the player goes to sleep. The chance of a random event to occur is 0.5% per day, and only one event can occur per night. The event does not change if the player reloads the day.
Anytime after the player has completed « Mythical Dream », there is a small chance a Goddess fairy will visit their farm at night to give a blessing.
If the player has any unwatered tiles at night, the fairy will water them; if the player has any immature crops on the farm, the fairy will bless them to make them instantly grow to their last stage.
If a fairy visits the farm, the player will get a message when they wake up: "Something water / bless your farm last night."

If the player has any [[crop|crop]]s or animal products in their [[shipping-bin|shipping bin]], there is a small chance a ghost will visit the farm to steal the shipped items. The player will not earn money for items the ghost steals. If a ghost visits, the player will get the following message when they wake up: "You felt an odd chill last night."

There is a chance a meteorite or a satellite will fall on the player's farm at night. The player will say they felt a large impact in the morning, and some satellite debris or a meteorite will be found on their farm. The types of meteorites the player can get depends on the quality of their pickaxe. The player can break the fallen debris with their [[pickaxe|pickaxe]].

mail.x: Mail is one of the ways the player communicates with characters both present and not present in the game. Most mail is sent to the player's mailbox in the morning (with some exception of [[cooking|cooking]] recipes that may arrive on the same day the player reaches the required [[friendship|friendship]] level with the character who sends the recipe, or when buying [[sturdy-computer|online]]). The mailbox is located outside the [[farmhouse|farmhouse]] on the right and can be interacted with.
Some letters contain attached items. These items can be accepted into the player's [[inventory|inventory]] after they read the letter.
Types of letters

Some letters are sent to the player randomly, others are received at fixed points in time or during main or secondary [[quest|quests]]. Some letters inform the player of news regarding the [[starlet-town|town]], new items available in stores, or new [[town-rank|Town rank]] reached. Over time, the player will also get letters from their family, their old employer, and Farmers Guild. Townfolk will send the player items or cooking recipes as the player gets closer to them. The player might also receive recurring letters, for example for passing out after 02:00.
Most of the letters the player has received can be found in the Journal menu (notes section).

getting-started.x: Coral Island is an open-ended traditional farming sim game set on a tropical island. Players are able to develop their farms and characters by growing crops, nurturing animals, fishing, foraging, exploring caves, cooking, and befriending locals.
The Players
[[player|Player]] can create their playable characters according to the customization available:
Controls
The player can [[controls|control]] the character’s movement using a keyboard and a mouse.
Energy
[[energy|Energy]] is required to carry out activities on the island. Players can find energy at the top left corner where a heart and green bar is located.

The energy decreases when players carry out the tasks and activities during the day. Once the player runs out of energy, they will return back to their house the next day. To replenish energy, players can eat consumable objects or non-poisonous food.
Health
[[health|Health]] is located at the top left of the UI right under Energy. Health only appears when players are at the mine or battle monsters.
Players lose health when they are hit by attacks. To replenish health (and energy), players can consume edible objects or non-poisonous food.
Skills
[[masteries|Skills]] are points players gain as they do various tasks and activities on the island. The more often players do the said activities, the more skill points they’ll have.
Skill points can be spent on a skill tree where each branch contains specific skills. You need to spend a certain amount of points to unlock the deeper branch of the skill tree.
Each branch of the skill tree corresponds to different skills and increases your proficiency for that particular skill area.
Game Time

[[game-time|Game Time]] is the number of hours where players can do various tasks on the island. The day starts at 6 A.M. and ends at 12 A.M. However, players can stay awake until 2 A.M. although there are consequences for staying up late.
Game Time Speed can be changed in the game settings.
Inventory
[[inventory|Inventory]] is where players store their items. Inventory allows players to immediately keep the items they find.
At the beginning of the game, players are given 15 slots for the inventory. Players can purchase more slots at [[sams-general-store|Sam's General Store]] by upgrading to a bigger bag.
First upgrade costs 500G.

controls.x: As for today, the player can only move and interact with objects using a keyboard and mouse, although controller support will soon be released.

energy.x: Energy is required to carry out activities on the island. Energy is consumed when the [[player|player]] uses the various [[tool|tools]] to complete tasks. If the player drops below 0 energy, they will collapse, being returned to the farmhouse and ending the in-game day.

Energy is restored at the beginning of every in-game day, as well as by eating [[consumables|consumable items]] such as [[cooking|cooked food]] and raw food ingredients or by resting at the [[hot-spring|hot spring]]. The player can also level various [[masteries|masteries]] to increase their total amount of energy and reduce the energy drained from using related tools.
The player starts the game with 450 energy, gaining more by leveling their masteries or consuming rare [[stamina-fruit|stamina fruit]].
The player can restore their energy by sleeping. However, sleeping will skip [[game-time|time]] to the following day.

It is recommended to sleep before 12 AM to gain full energy when the player wakes up the next day. The player is automatically brought back to the farmhouse when they are awake past 2 AM, and their energy bar will not be at its maximum level.

health.x: Health is located at the top left of the UI, right under [[energy|Energy]]. Players lose health when they are hit by attacks by [[monster|monsters]] in the [[cavern|mine]], being exposed to bombs' explosion, or due to some [[buff|debuff]] such as poison or burn. To replenish health (and [[energy|energy]]), players can consume [[consumables|consumables]].
If health is dropped to zero, the player will be teleported to the mine entrance if they're inside mine, or restored with 1 health if outside the mine.

There are two ways to permanently increase the player's maximum health points; consuming a [[wellness-fruit|Wellness fruit]] and by gaining [[masteries|mastery]] points. Consuming a wellness fruit will permanently increase maximum health points by 45. Gaining a mastery point will increase the player's maximum health by 3 points.

game-time.x: Game time is the number of hours where the player can do various tasks on the island. The day starts at 6:00 and ends at 23:59 (11:59PM). Players can stay awake until 2:00 - though there are consequences for staying up late.

Time in Coral Island passes at a rate of 1 in-game hour per 45 real world seconds or 1,080 real world seconds per 24 in-game hours by default. The passage of time is paused when the player is viewing a cutscene or talking to a townie, or when they are accessing any of the game's menus.

The game speed can be changed from the options menu, reducing the tick rate by up to 50% and thus increase the amount of time it takes for a single hour in-game to pass to 67.5 real world seconds from the default 45 real world seconds per in-game hour.
Days in Coral Island pass in various stages that influence the lighting, music, and appearances of many fish, insects, and sea critters.

The clock in the upper right corner of the UI displays an icon representing Daytime during 6h – 17:50h (6:00AM-5:50PM) and Nighttime during 18h – 23:50h (6:00PM-11:50PM). Insects and sea critters spawn and despawn based on these divisions of the day.
Fish appearances are instead divided into four times of day:
The times are visible on the Sturdy Computer if the Fishing Component is researched.
The exact timing of the transitions may vary from season to season, with longer daylight hours in the summer and longer nights in the winter.

All shops and townies in Coral Island abide by schedules based on the in-game time, in addition to day of the week, season and weather. Most shops will open or close according to the hour, while townies may travel to certain locations or perform certain tasks depending on the time.
Players will wake up with at least as much energy as they had when they went to bed. If they sleep early, their energy bar will be refilled up to certain levels.

Players who sleep before 12:00 will wake up with a full energy bar. Sleeping between 12:00 and just before 01:00 will refill the energy bar to between 75% and 95%, depending on the exact time the player slept. Sleeping at 01:00 or later will only refill the energy bar to 50% (rounded up). Players who stay awake past 2:00 will collapse and be automatically brought back to the farmhouse with their energy bars only partially refilled and a small fee (5% of the player's money, up to 2,000 ) taken from their wallet.
The player will wake up at 6:00 regardless of what time they went to bed.

inventory.x: Inventory is where the player stores their items. Inventory allows the player to immediately keep the items they find. At the beginning of the game, the player is given 15 slots for the inventory. Players can purchase more slots at [[sams-general-store|Sam's General store]].

Two slots are allotted for buffs. One is from food and the other is from drink. You may only have one buff per type at a time. Eating/drinking another consumable of the same type will replace the previous buff.

Four slots are allotted for equipment. The lower two are for equipping rings, each with its own enhancement effect. The upper left slot is for applying fish bait to the players fishing pole. The upper right slot is for flowers; the player's appearance will update depending on the flower.

Outfit has six slots to arrange an outfit to dress the player with: top, bottom, hat, glasses, back, and footwear. It is worthy to note that the tops slot is also used to equip the pre-made whole outfits.
Used for discarding items from the inventory to free up space for new items. Items placed in this slot will be disposed of immediately and will not be recoverable.

tool.x: Tools are items that allow [[player|player]]s to do activities and tasks around the island. The player can carry around tools by storing them in their [[inventory|inventory]]. To use a tool, it needs to be selected (highlighted) in the tool bar.

The player can upgrade their tools by leaving them at [[sanchez-brothers-blacksmith|Sanchez Brothers Blacksmith]] and waiting for several days. Each upgrade requires different upgrade materials, with higher level upgrades requiring more money and rarer materials. The higher the upgrade level, the more effective the tool becomes. On top of that some tools can be [[enchanting|enchanted]] at Giants village.

Some tools have overlapping capability, such as removing equipment which can be done by [[axe|axe]] or [[pickaxe|pickaxe]], removing weeds which can be done by [[axe|axe]], [[pickaxe|pickaxe]], or [[scythe|scythe]], and so on.
Hoe
[[hoe|Hoe]] is mainly used to prepare soil for [[farming|farming]], dig out [[clover|clovers]], or dig out dirt for random items.
Axe
[[axe|Axe]] is mainly used to chop [[trees|trees]] and harvest giant [[crop|crop]]s.
Pickaxe
[[pickaxe|Pickaxe]] is mainly used to break regular rocks, boulders, and meteorite.
Scythe
[[scythe|Scythe]] is mainly used to destroy trash.
Watering can
[[watering-can|Watering can]] is used to water tilled soil on the farm.
Fishing pole
[[fishing-pole|Fishing pole]] is used to [[fishing|catch fish]] in any body of water.
Bug net
[[bug-net|Bug net]] is used to catch [[insect|insect]]s and [[sea-critter|ocean critters]].
Lumina wand
[[lumina-wand|Lumina wand]] is used to provide sunlight to underwater crops on their underwater farm.

weapon.x: Weapons are tools used to attack and fend off monsters. Unlike the regular tools used for farming, weapons do not consume stamina to use and cannot be upgraded or enchanted. Instead, new weapons can be purchased from the [[band-of-smiles|Band of Smiles]]. Unlike [[trinket|trinket]]s, weapons can't be equipped, but used the same way [[tool|tools]] are used.
Each weapon has a different set of stats, with different types of weapons being more effective in certain areas such as spears having larger range or hammers dealing heavier damage.

weapon.x: Swords are well-balanced weapons that offer decent range, attack speed, and damage. The sword's secondary ability allows players to use a special spinning attack once it's fully charged. Charge for swords is accumulated by striking enemies enough times. The spin deals .75x the sword's normal damage but can hit any enemies around the player multiple times.
All swords have a 3-hit combo that deals 1.5x the normal damage on its final hit.

weapon.x: Shields sacrifice some of their offensive ability for increased defense and are the only weapons to consistently grant a defense bonus when equipped. The shield's secondary ability allows the player to completely block an enemy's attack and retaliate with a powerful shield bash for 2.5x the shield's normal damage.
All shields have a 2-hit combo with no change in damage.

Spears are situated between swords and shields in offensive ability, but have the longest reach of the available weapons. This is further extended by the spear's secondary ability allowing the player to throw the spear several meters ahead of them for 0.5x the spear's normal damage. Unlike other weapons' secondary abilities, the spear can be thrown without needing to be charged in any way, but requires a one second delay between throws.
All spears have a 2-hit combo that deals 0.5x damage on the second hit.

Hammers are the slowest and most damaging weapons available. The hammer's secondary ability allows the player to hold down the secondary attack button to manually charge a heavy swing that will also stun enemies struck by it, preventing them from moving for a few seconds. The damage done by a charged swing depends on the level of charge is able to build on it:
The amount of charge a hammer is able to build up depends on the specific weapon.
All hammers are unable to combo, and can only deal one hit at a time.

artifact.x: Artifacts are valuable ancient items that can be found through various means. Artifacts can be donated to the [[museum|Museum]] to complete the collection. Some artifacts can also be used for quests and various tasks.
In addition to being found in coffers, most artifacts can also be purchased at the [[black-market|Black Market]] for an increased price.

Each artifact can be donated to the museum once for 3 points Museum. Completing donation for all 78 artifacts will also earn 40 points Museum as well as unique rewards from museum and succès « Memento Of The Past ». Artifacts can be duplicated through [[slime-of-replication|slime of replication]] and can also be sold or [[gift|gift]]ed.
Artifacts are are considered universally neutral gifts.

As of v0.3, artifacts can also be used as fuel for the enchanting system with certain artifacts being worth a set amount of points based on their rarity. A list of all items that can be used for enchanting and their point values can be found on the [[enchanting|Enchanting]] page.
4 artifacts of any type are needed for the Master Slime section of the [[guardian-mural|Guardian Mural]] altar.

The primary way of obtaining artifacts is opening coffers: the special chests that can be opened at [[sanchez-brothers-blacksmith|Sanchez Brothers Blacksmith]] for 20 or per piece. Coffers are a rare drop for clearing [[trash|trash]] with a [[scythe|scythe]] on the island or on the [[ocean|ocean]] floor, or by tilling soil or sand with a [[hoe|hoe]]. Rarely, they can be obtained by [[fishing|fishing]] on the main map as well.

gem.x: Gems are items that can be found down in the [[cavern|Cavern]] or obtained by opening . Gems are rare and valuable and can be donated to the [[museum|museum]] to complete the gem collection. The player can also sell gems for money or use them for [[enchanting|enchanting]] or gifts.

Gems can be duplicated through [[slime-of-replication|slime of replication]] and can also be sold or gifted.

Gems are considered universally liked gifts with some exceptions: [[archie|Archie]] and the [[chieftain|Chieftain]] love all gems and [[pablo|Pablo]] is neutral towards them. Additionally, several townsfolk love or hate certain gems.

Geodes need to be opened at [[sanchez-brothers-blacksmith|Sanchez Brothers Blacksmith]] instead. Cracking a geode open costs 20 or per piece. consumables.x: Consumables are items that can be consumed, generally to restore health or stamina, or items that have some buff or debuff effect. Consumables can be obtained from crafting, cooking, collecting animal products, farming, foraging, producing through artisan equipment, or buying from shop.

trees.x: Wild trees can be found on the [[farm|farm]] and other world map areas. These trees can be chopped with an [[axe|axe]] and drop several items for the player depending on the type and the age of the tree. Although all trees drop several universal items like [[wood|wood]] or [[sap|sap]], they also produce different types of goods.
Logging

In order to chop a tree, the player needs a tool. Tree seeds and seedlings can be chopped by most tools like axe, [[hoe|hoe]], [[pickaxe|pickaxe]], or [[scythe|scythe]], while more mature trees can only be chopped with an axe. Old stumps and large logs require a stronger updated axe.
Skills and experience

Chopping trees earns the player experience points in their [[foraging|foraging]] [[masteries|mastery]]. As the player improves their foraging mastery, they will be able to unlock [[foraging|skills]] that allow them to improve their chances of rarer drops when logging.
Tapping

The player can place a [[tap|tap]] on any mature wild tree to start collecting its sap to turn it into [[artisan-product|artisan products]]. All products produced by tapping take three days to make; the result depends on the type of tree the player taps.
Types of trees and drops

Three types of wild trees exist in the game: oak, maple, and pine. All trees drop the same items when chopped down, with only variation being the type of seeds they drop. foraging.x: Foraging, also called scavenging or gathering, is one of the [[masteries|masteries]] that involves the player gathering items in the wild on Coral Island and cutting [[trees|trees]]. The player can use the items for various things, from [[gift|gift]]s to [[cooking|cooking]] to selling them for money.
Foraging mastery

The player can increase their foraging mastery level by cutting down trees and regularly gathering items on the island. Most of these actions give the player foraging experience; as the player obtains more experience, their foraging mastery level improve, allowing them to unlock new [[crafting|crafting]] recipes and useful skills.
Experience

The player's actions that depend on and increase their foraging mastery level are detailed below. Foraging [[diving|ocean scavengables]] will only give [[diving|diving]] experience. Destroying trees using bombs will also provide points. Note that these are referring to [[trees|trees]] growth state and not referring to [[fruit-plant|fruit plants]] or [[fruit-tree|fruit trees]]. Gathering [[coconut-group|any coconut]] will not provide foraging points.

Reaching a new level in foraging mastery grants the player new crafting recipes when they go to sleep to end their day.
Skills

Every other foraging mastery level gained allows the player to unlock one skill. The player will be able to unlock up to five skills by leveling up. The last skill can be unlocked by purchasing [[merit-points|foraging elixir]].

Only wild trees are affected, the five types of wild trees available are [[maple-tree|maple]], [[oak-tree|oak]], [[pine-tree|pine]], [[mahogany-tree|mahogany]], and [[poplar-tree|poplar]].

crop.x: Crops are plants that the player can grow from [[crop|Seeds]] on their [[farm|farm]] to sell for profit, process into [[artisan-product|artisan products]] or [[cooking|cooked dishes]], consume to restore [[health|health]] and [[energy|energy]], or give to other characters as gifts.

Crops are generally seasonal, meaning they can only be planted and will only grow during their specified season and die when the season changes. Some crops (e.g. [[hot-pepper|Hot pepper]]) are multi-seasonal, and can be planted across multiple seasons. Crops can be further processed into artisan products using [[artisan-product|artisan equipment]]. Crops may also be used as ingredients in [[cooking|cooking]].

This page refers only to seed crops that are planted in 1×1 areas. For larger and longer lived crops, see [[fruit-plant|fruit plant]]s or [[fruit-tree|fruit tree]]s, or [[all-plant|all plant]]s for overall.
Mechanics
Obtaining seeds
A variety of seeds can be purchased at [[sams-general-store|Sam's General Store]]. The store selection depends on the current [[calendar|season]] and the player's [[town-rank|town rank]].
The player can occasionally obtain [[wild-seeds|wild seeds]] while tilling soil or cutting weeds or grass. These wild seeds will turn into a random seasonal crop when sown.
[[ocean-crops|Ocean crops]] are available after the player completes the quest « One of us » and reaches town rank A. Note that some mechanics might differ for ocean crops.
Basics

Crops can only be planted on the player's farm into soil tilled by a [[hoe|hoe]]. Tilling soil consumes the player's energy. Once the soil is tilled, the player can place [[fertilizer|fertilizer]] and any seed into that square; all crops currently available in the game take up a 1×1 area. The tile may then be watered using a [[watering-can|watering can]]; an action that also consumes the player's energy. A planted and watered seed will start growing.

Crops have to be watered can every day with the exception of [[weather|rainy days]], as the rain will water the plant. Watered crops will grow the next day. Unwatered crops will not grow the next day, but will not wither until the season change. When crops are ready to harvest, the player can do it manually or by using a [[scythe|scythe]].
Most crops can be walked through after they are planted and even after they have matured. Only one crop, [[peas|Peas]], currently grows on a trellis and cannot be walked through once it is planted.
Any crop can be removed from its tile during any growth stage by hitting it with a [[pickaxe|pickaxe]].
Growth and regrowth times

Every crop takes a specific number of days to grow and goes through a specific number of growth stages. These growth times include the day the seed is first planted and watered. Meaning, if a crop needs 10 days to grow and planted on day 1, it'll be ready to be harvested on day 11, provided they are still watered everyday from day 1 to day 10. Some [[farming|farming]] mastery skills give the player a chance to speed up the crop growth; a Flash fertilizer can also be used prior to planting to increase the growth rate.

Most crops disappear after they are harvested; however, some crops will regrow after each harvest, provided they are still watered everyday. The pattern persists until the crop is uprooted or until the season change that kills the crop.
These are the list of crops that can regrow
Quality

The [[laboratory|Laboratory]] offers upgrade to the player's seeds, plants, fruit trees, and hay. Each upgrade costs some essence produced from [[kelp|kelps]] using the [[extractor|Extractor]] and game money.

Upgrades purchased at the laboratory apply to all seeds in the player's inventory or planted on the farm and all future seed purchases with no increase in price. Once upgraded, the base quality of all seed crop produce will increase.
Crows

Every morning, there is a 60% chance a crop will be eaten by a crow if there is at least 12 crops growing on the farm and there is no [[scarecrow|scarecrow]] protecting them. Once a crow eats a crop, that crop disappears completely; the player can pick up some wild seeds at the footprints the crow has left.
The first time a crow eats a crop, the « Crows be gone » will be initiated.
Giant crops
Some crops planted in a 3×3 pattern have a small (5%) chance to turn into a giant crop if left unharvested. Only eight crops in the game can become giant.

Unlike regular crops, giant crops cannot be harvested manually or with a scythe and require an [[axe|axe]]. Each giant crop will yield 17 to 21 regular sized crops when harvested, but will destroy crops that would usually allow multiple harvests in the process. Giant crop will stay as it is, does not require water, and will not even wither off season, until they are harvested.
Seasonal crops

Only [[snowdrop|snowdrop]] and [[radish|radish]] are being sold throughout the seasons they can be planted.

[[hot-pepper|Hot pepper]], [[lily-flower|lily]] and [[cotton|cotton]] seeds are not available at [[sams-general-store|Sam's General Store]] in fall and must be purchased during summer (Hot pepper, lily) or winter (cotton).

See [[fruit-plant|Fruit plant]]s for the two-season crops that are in the game.
Mechanics
Obtaining saplings
A variety of saplings will be available for purchase at [[sams-general-store|Sam's General Store]] once the player reaches [[town-rank|town rank]] C.
Basics
Fruit trees do not require tilled soil nor watering and can not be [[fertilizer|fertilized]].
Fruit trees require empty surrounding of 5x5 tiles to be to be planted.

When fruit trees are ready to harvest, the player must manually harvest the tree.
Any fruit tree can be removed from its tiles during any growth stage by hitting it with an [[axe|axe]].
Growth and regrowth times
Every fruit tree takes 28 days to grow and goes through a specific number of growth stages. These growth times include the day the sapling is first planted.
All fruit on fruit trees will regrow after each harvest. The pattern persists until the fruit tree is cut down or until the season change that ends the harvesting period.
Some [[farming|farming]] mastery skills give the player a chance to speed up the plant growth;

Once the trees are fully grown and enter their harvesting season, they will initialize on day 1 and produce fruits every 4 days. If a tree is mature at the start of its harvest season, fruits can be harvested on day 5, day 9, day 13, day 17, day 21, day 25 of the particular season.
Quality

The [[laboratory|Laboratory]] offers upgrade to the player's seeds, plants, fruit trees, and hay. Each upgrade costs some essence produced from [[kelp|kelps]] using the [[extractor|Extractor]] and game money.

Upgrades purchased at the laboratory apply to all saplings in the player's inventory or planted on the farm and all future sapling purchases with no increase in price. Once upgraded, there will be higher chance in getting higher quality of all fruit tree produce.

A tile may then be watered using a [[watering-can|watering can]]; the action consumes the player's energy. A planted and watered seedling will start growing.

Meaning, if a seedling is planted on day 1, it'll be ready to be harvested on day 11, provided they are still watered everyday from day 1 to day 10.

shipping-bin.x: The shipping bin is the medium that allows the player to sell items they grow or produce on the [[farm|farm]], [[foraging|find in the wild]], or catch.

The shipping bin is located next to the player's [[farmhouse|farmhouse]], the player will be able to see it as they are heading down to Starlet Town. The items placed into the shipping bin will be sold at the end of the day, and the gold will be added to the player's money total at the start of the next game day.
It is possible for the player to take back items that they put in the shipping bin as long as it is still the same day.

If the player has any [[crop|crops]] or animal products in their shipping bin at the end of the day, there is a 0.5% chance a [[random-event|random event]] will occur with a ghost showing up at the farm and stealing items from the shipping bin. The player will not earn money for items the ghost steals.

farm-animal.x: Farm animals provide players with resources that can be processed into artisan products or sold directly. All farm animals require players to build a farm building to house them, such as a [[coop|coop]] or a [[barn|barn]], before the purchase of farm animals. Farm animals can be purchased at the [[ranch|Ranch]].
[[pet|Pets]] and [[mythical-pets|Mythical Pets]] are types of animal companions that are separate from standard farm animals.
General mechanics
Obtaining animals
All farm animals can be purchased at the [[ranch|Ranch]]. The store's selection depends on the player's [[town-rank|town rank]] and the presence of any barns or coops on the farm.
Caring
Feeding

Animals can be fed manually by placing [[hay|hay]] on the feeder, or automatically by [[auto-feeder|auto feeder]] (with hay in the [[silo|silo]]). There is 25% chance for animal feed to stay filled the next day if Animal Feed is learned. Animals can also be let outside with grass on sunny days. Letting animals outside on rainy days will worsen their mood. Animals that are let outside will automatically return home at the end of the day.
Fodder upgrade

The [[laboratory|Laboratory]] offers upgrade to the quality of the player's seeds, plants, fruit trees, and hay. Each upgrade costs some essence produced from [[kelp|kelps]] using the [[extractor|Extractor]] and game money. Each upgrade requires 2 days without the need of manually collecting the upgrade unlike upgrading tools.

Upgrades purchased at the laboratory apply to all hay in the player's inventory and all future hay purchases with no increase in price. Once upgraded, there will be higher chance to obtain higher quality for all animal products. There is an additional of 10% chance for higher quality if Quality Product is learned.
Health

Animals can become sick if they are not fed, or if they have been hot or cold during summer or winter due to no [[temperature-machine|temperature machine]] installed in the animal house. If it's due to the latter, 1 animal can be affected in animal house level 1 and 2 animals can be affected in animal house level 2. The longer the consecutive days of being not taken care because of those reasons, the higher the chance to get sick.

When an animal is sick, it will not produce nor gain friendship points and will require [[animal-medicine|animal medicine]] for instant recovery, or up to 4 days for manual recovery. The first time animal get sick, [[jack|Jack]] will send an [[animal-medicine|animal medicine]] in the mail.
Hearts & mood

Similar to [[friendship|befriending characters]], animals have heart level of maximum 10, and friendship points required to level up the heart level. On top of that, it has 3 different mood level, bad mood, neutral and happy. Hearts and mood will impact the size/type of their products. Unlike characters, farm animals have the same friendship points required for each heart level although the exact points is currently unknown.

These are the factors that affect heart points and mood. Animal house size, being petted, being fed, fodder quality, being affected by weather outside (plus rate during good weather, minus during bad weather), being in good temperature.

The player can only adopt a maximum of three pets as of now, and the pets chosen can never be returned or changed. Although every pet from the [[pet-shelter|Pet shelter]] has a preset name, the pets can be renamed upon adoption.

Once the the player has adopted a pet, [[paul|Paul]] and [[anne|Anne]] will bring the pet to the player the following morning. A pet does not require food or water.

artisan-product.x: Artisan products, or artisan goods, are items that are produced using artisan equipment by processing raw [[crop|crop]]s, [[foraging|foraged items]], or animal products. Each artisan piece of equipment produces different goods of different qualities, depending on the quality of the ingredients.
Artisan products are produced in the span of a few hours to days and usually sell for more than the raw ingredients they are produced from.
Overview

In order to make artisan products, the player has to obtain artisan equipment first. The equipment is unlocked by leveling up the player's basic [[masteries|masteries]] level. Once the player obtains the recipe, they can [[crafting|craft]] it and place it on their [[farm|farm]], and then load it with raw items to start producing. The player can have as many artisan equipment as they would like, provided they have the required materials and space to place them. The equipment can be placed on the farm or in the [[shed|shed]].

Each artisan product consumes one input item and takes from an hour to several days to produce depending on the machine and item used. The resulting quality depends on the quality of the input item used.
Artisan equipment
Artisan products by artisan equipment
Aging barrel
An [[aging-barrel|aging barrel]] produces aged, preserved, fermented or alcoholic products. It is unlocked by reaching level 10 in [[farming|Farming]] mastery.
Bee house
A [[bee-house|bee house]] produces honey from [[flower|flowers]]. It is unlocked by reaching level 6 in [[catching|Bug catching]] mastery.
Cheese press
A [[cheese-press|cheese press]] makes cheese. It is unlocked by reaching level 4 in [[ranching|Ranching]] mastery.
Dehydrator
A [[dehydrator|dehydrator]] removes the moisture from fruits and vegetables. It is unlocked by reaching level 4 in [[diving|Diving]] mastery.
Keg

fishing.x: Proficiency

The higher the player's fishing level is, the less energy it costs to use the fishing pole. Using [[consumables|consumables]] that grant a [[buff|fishing proficiency buff]] can temporarily further reduce the stamina cost.
Fishing controls

Most bodies of water in the game can be fished from. Basic fishing is done by casting the end of the fishing line into a body of water. The player casts the fishing rod by holding the right mouse button, then releasing it; as the player holds down the button, their casting gauge fills. The higher the cast number when the player releases the button, the further the bobber will fly. Additionally, the cast length affects the player's chances to catch trash and rarer fish.

Once the line is cast, the player needs to wait until a fish bites. Once a fish bites, the fishing mini-game starts immediately. During the mini-game, the player's objective is to reel the fish in by holding or tapping the left mouse button while avoiding the tension to rise enough for the fish to snap the line. Once the player reels the fish in, they are shown what species it is and its size in centimeters, and the fish gets added to their [[inventory|inventory]].
Mechanics
Cast length

The length of the cast when fishing can influence the fish's rarity and size, as well as the odds of catching trash, and there is a constant small chance of catching a rare item like a geode or coffer. Quality of [[fishing-pole|fishing pole]] affects max cast length and some other parameters that affects fishing efficiency.
For most spawn locations, the distribution is:
*Example, if cast length is 6, the chance of getting common fish is ~19%. If cast length is 1, the chance of getting large fish is ~6.5%.
Trash and treasures
While fishing, there's still at least 5% chance to find [[trash|trash]] or [[flyer|flyer]] even at max cast length. There's also 0.05% chance to find treasure at any cast length.
Rarity of fish

So far rarity of fish can't be influenced during fishing. However, there are some variant of fish that can be fished in the mines with lower rarity compared to their regular counterpart. There are 4 rarity group:
Legendary fish will take 4 days to breed in [[fish-pond|fish pond]] while the rest will only take 2 days.
Size of fish
Cast length and bait can influence fish's size during fishing. There are 3 size group:
Bait

Bait can be attached to a fishing pole using the equipable slot for it in the player's inventory. Baits can be used to increase the chance catching different size of fish. Bait can be crafted or can also be purchased from the [[beach-shack|Beach Shack]].
Fish patterns
All fish are assigned one of a few possible swim patterns that can be observed when they're on the line. The pattern can be used to further narrow down the kind of fish that is on the hook.

can also be used to quickly destroy trash found underwater, but lack the chance of activating mining skills. A [[pickaxe|pickaxe]] is required to destroy sandstone deposits on the ocean floor, but doesn't affect the Diving skill.

They can also catch underwater [[sea-critter|critter]]s with their [[bug-net|bug net]], cut seaweed, or collect that spawn on the ground.

Healing corals earns the player points Ocean, improves the quality of fish caught, and progresses one of the main [[quest|quest]]s of the game. It can also open previously inaccessible underwater areas by cleaning the oil from the environment.

quest.x: Quests are specific events that earn players rewards or unlocked new storylines. Quests are divided into main quests, side quests, and errands in Coral Island.
Errands

Errands are randomized, time-limited quests that the player can take on from the job boards in [[starlet-town|Starlet Town]], [[band-of-smiles|Band of Smiles Hideout]], and the [[merfolk-kingdom|Merfolk Kingdom]]. Once accepted, most errands must be completed in two days - the day the quest is accepted and the next - with the exception of Grow Me errands which give the player the length of time needed to grow the item plus one day to harvest and deliver it. Completing an errand rewards the player with an amount of money dependent on the type of errand and any items delivered.

Up to one errand may be available each day for pickup at each of the job boards. Once a player accepts an errand from the [[starlet-town|Starlet Town]] job board, further errands will not appear at this board until the current errand is either completed or abandoned. In contrast, [[band-of-smiles|Band of Smiles Hideout]] errands may continue to appear even if one is active.
Completing many errands for the Band of Smiles can also unlock new items from the guild store.
Types of errands
There are four types of errands to choose from, two for each of the job boards available.

r: Town Courier errands encompass any request by an available townie for a specified item. This item can be: * A seasonal fruit, vegetable, or flower available at the player's town rank * An animal product if the player has the required building and town rank needed to purchase the animal Completion of Town Courier errands rewards the player with three times the requested item's base sell price as well as 250 points Heart with the townie that requested it. Townies will only request items that they are at least neutral or more favorable of. All townies - children and adults - are able to post requests. [[nina|Nina]] is only able to post requests when she visits in [[summer|Summer]].

Grow Me Something errands encompass all requests to grow a new specified product for delivery to an available townie. This item can be any seasonal fruit, vegetable, or flower available at the player's town rank.  Completion of Grow Me Something errands rewards the player with two times the requested item's base sell price as well as 250 points Heart with the townie that requested it. Townies will only request items that they are at least neutral or more favorable of. All townies - children and adults - are able to post requests. [[nina|Nina]] is only able to post requests when she visits in [[summer|Summer]].  Grow Me Something errands have a longer time limit than other errands, allowing for the length of time for the product to grow plus one day for harvest and delivery.

B.O.S. Requests encompass all requests by Band of Smiles members for a specified item. This item can be: * 3 to 10 pieces of stone, coal, or ore available to the mines the player has access to * 2 to 10 metal bars available to the mines the player has access to * 3 to 5 bottles of monster or elemental essence available to the mines the player has access to * 2 to 5 pieces of monster loot depending on the depths the player has reached and the mines the player has access to Completion of B.0.S. Request errands rewards the player with three times the requested item's base sell price as well as 250 points Heart with the BOS member that requested it, if applicable.

Slay errands encompass all requests by Band of Smiles members to hunt a number of monsters. These quests can require slaying: * 10 to 20 of an element of monsters available to the mines the player has access to * 1 to 10 of a specific species and element of monster depending on the depths the player has reached and the mines the player has access to Completion of Slay errands rewards the player with an amount of gold determined by the type of errand undertaken - 500 for an element-based errand, or 300-900 for a specific species. Slay errands do not reward friendship for completion.

friendship.x: The player can form a bond of friendship with [[townies|townies]], [[giant|giant]]s and [[merfolk|merfolk]]. Getting to know these characters by exchanging stories and triggering dialog cutscenes will allow the player character and NPCs to become closer. Friendship does not decay over time.

Currently, the player can sometimes raise their heart level with some [[extras|strangers]] as well by having conversations with them. There are no known consequences for the rise of these heart levels so far.
Heart points

The game interface displays the player's heart points, or friendship points, with an NPC through a heart gauge. Talking to other characters and giving them gifts causes that character's heart gauge to rise.

Regular, non-dateable characters have a maximum heart level of 10. On the other hand, it is not possible to raise the heart level of dateable characters beyond 8 without the player being in a committed relationship with them. That state is triggred by giving the [[locket|Locket]] to the romanceable character. At that point, the maximum heart level of 10 for that romanceable character unlocks. The gift of the Locket is not exclusive. The player can give the Locket to any dateable character with whom they reach a heart level of 8 and form a relationship with them.
Furthermore, once the player has wed the character in question, that character's maximum heart level rises to 15. Currently, it is only possible to have one spouse.
Heart events
Gaining heart levels with each character will unlock unique events. The events' triggers and conditions vary depending on the character. Refer to each character's event information for more details.
Earning heart points
The player can earn points Heart with characters by chatting with them daily and giving them gifts.
Chatting

The player can chat with each character to get 35 points Heart per day. During a festival, chatting may earn 0, 35, 50, or 85 points Heart, unless the player has already talked to that character before the festival on that day. The player can only cause a character's friendship points to rise once per day. The player can chat with a character as many times as they want until their lines for the day are exhausted, but this will not cause the amount of friendship points to rise more than once on that day.

The characters have a variety of dialog cutscenes that the player can unlock. These include generic dialog, dialog that is specific to the character's current location, dialog that is specific to the current season, or dialog that is specific to the player's heart level towards them at that moment. The characters can react to some in-game story events, such as the [[pufferfish-drilling-corp|Pufferfish Drilling Corp]] arriving into town, or the [[museum|Museum]] expanding after a successful Pickstarter campaign. Some characters will also make a comment if they see the player holding a [[weapon|weapon]], wearing a [[pufferfish-farmer-outfit|Pufferfish farmer outfit]], a [[chicken-suit|Chicken suit]], or a [[panda-outfit|Panda outfit]], or wearing no [[clothing|clothes]] at all. Additionally, there is always a small chance for the player to witness cutscenes of very personal and intimate scenes between NPCs. These cutscenes do not repeat.
Hangout

The player can ask certain characters for a hangout. The request can only be made while the player's hands are empty. The hangouts can be regular hangouts with most NPC's, as well as dates with romantic interests. Some hangout locations have weather requirements or need to be unlocked for the player to visit them.
Gifting
See also: [[gift-preferences|Gift preferences]] page for a sortable list of all characters and their individual gift preferences

Gifting is a primary mechanic of earning points Heart with characters. The player can give each character up to two gifts per one in-game week. One additional gift is allowed on a character's birthday, regardless of what else the player has given them that week. In order to gift an item, the player needs to place it in their [[inventory|inventory]] hotbar and interact with the character they want to gift the item to.

Most items in the game, such as [[foraging|scavengeables]], [[crop|crop]]s, [[fish|fish]], [[insect|insects]], [[artisan-product|artisan products]], [[cooking|meals]], and even [[trash|trash]], can be gifted. Each character has their individual gift preferences: they can love, like, dislike or hate the gift, or have no reaction to it. Characters will have different interactions with the player based on their preference towards the item. The more the character likes the gift, the bigger the points Heart gain. Dislike and hated items on the other hand have negative effects on the amount points Heart held towards that character. However, the player's heart level towards a character can never sink lower than the minimum number of points required for their current friendship level*.
Gifting points

*For example, the player has reached 4 cœur(s)/heart level 4 with Ben and is having 1550 points Heart. As from table above, 1500 points Heart is required for 4 cœur(s)/heart level 4. If at this time Ben is given something he dislike, the friendship point will decrease to 1515, but if at that time he was given something he hate, the friendship point will not decrease and stay at 1550 as 1550-70 is 1480 and 1480 is below the friendship points required for that level which is 1500. Or to summarize, the heart level will stay at 4 cœur(s)/heart level 4 and will not go back to 3 cœur(s)/heart level 3.
Item multiplier
On top of that, there is a multiplier for items of better quality.
Note that fractions will be rounded down.
Birthday multiplier

It doesn't stop here, if the player presents a gift to an NPC during their birthday, they will earn five times the regular amount of points for the action. In other words, if the character gives a loved item (140) of osmium quality (which multiplies by 2), during birthday (which multiplies by 5), it will amount to 140 * 2 * 5, or 1,400 points Heart counted towards that character. Note that some characters do not celebrate their birthday, so the birthday multiplier will never apply to them.
Errands
Townies may randomly make request for errands. Completing the errand will earn 250 points Heart towards that character. See [[quest|Errands]].
Events

There are certain milestones that provide points Heart to all [[townies|townies]]. However, these points won't be retrospectively added to townies the player haven't met. The points mechanics will be revisited once merfolk friendship is available to check whether those are awarded to merfolk as well. Currently, [[giant|Giant]]s are not affected by these points
One time
Repeatable
Quests
Some minority of the [[quest|main quests]] also provide points Heart to certain character upon completion.

The [[quest|mail side quests]] will set the heart level to 1 with 300 points Heart towards the requestor when the heart level is 1 or below. Meaning, if the friendship points are below 300 it will be boosted to 300, reaching heart level 1, however, if the friendship points are already reaching the next level, e.g. 630, it will reset back to 300.
Romance

Players are able to [[romance|date]], and eventually marry, one of the 25 dateable characters and start a family with them. In order to do so, players must reach a certain level of friendship and unlock the character's story. Romance is not restricted to any gender.
Badges
Various interaction can earn some [[badges|badges]]. Refer to the page for exact requirement.

weather.x: Coral Island offers players a dynamic weather system that mirrors real-world conditions. Players may experience sunny days, stormy weather, rain showers, snowy weather, and windy breezes as they explore on the island.
Five weather conditions currently exist on Coral Island. Players can view the next day's weather through the weather forecast channel on the [[television|television]].

r: Sunny weather has no effect on the [[farm|farm]] or the player. Expect a bright and vivid day.
Windy weather has no direct effect on the farm or the player, but it does add a visual effect to farm [[crop|crops]] and [[trees|trees]]. They sway back and forth under this weather condition.
Stormy weather waters all crops on the farm. In addition to wet floors and buildings, stormy weather implements sounds of thunder and windy effects.
Snowy weather negates crop growth on the farm.
Like stormy weather, rainy weather waters all crops on the farms and makes floors and buildings appear wet. The only difference is the removal of thunder and lightning sounds,

i: Certain [[fish|fish]] can only be caught under specific weather conditions. See: ([[fish|Fish]])
Under windy conditions, it is stated that pollen will be abundant. [[charles|Charles]] has a pollen allergy, and it is unknown if this weather condition affects his dialogue.
The weather for the following day can be changed using a [[weather-conch|Weather conch]].

festival.x: Festivals are held every season and on different days. There are a total of 8 festivals held on Coral Island, each season has two festivals.
Overview

The player will be notified about the festival one day before the event starts. The Player’s attendance at festivals are not mandatory. To participate in the festivals, the player must enter the festivals’ locations within the appointed festivals’ time.

festival.x: Spring Festivals & Events
Cherry Blossom Potluck - Day 10

This festival takes place at [[alun-alun-square|Alun-Alun Square]], which is east of the [[lake|Lake]]. The festival starts at 9:00 and ends at 14:00. Interacting with the festival orbs triggers the conclusion of the festival. The Player can contribute to the potluck with an ingredient of their choice, by adding it to the pot at the east end of the festival area. By talking to [[connor|Connor]] after contributing, the main event will start.

The "main event" consists in tasting the potluck. [[judge-ross|Judge Ross]] actually performs the test. Players can also take part in a sack race like minigame, located in the southwest of the festival. A shop, the Cherry Blossom Shop, is located in the north of the festival. Some of its items are rare items.
The festival ends if the player leaves the festival area. The player will then spawn in front of their house at 21:00.
Tree Planting Festival - Day 21

The Tree Planting Festival is the second celebration of the year and takes place on the 21st of every [[spring|Spring]]. The [[festival|festival]] meet up is available from 8am to 2pm and is triggered by entering the area near the [[ranch|ranch]]. The main activity is also associated with 3 quests, starting with [[quest|Tree Planting Festival I side quest]]. The player can only gain merit points for completing the main activity 3 different times. There is also a booth with farming supplies.
To end the festival, the player will need to go towards the orb to the south. The player will then spawn in front of their house at 21:00.
Summer Festivals & Events
Animal Festival - Day 12

This festival takes place in the [[starlet-town|Starlet Town]] center, starting between 9:00 - 14:00. This festival is about celebrating the animals on Coral Island, and includes several animal themed games. The [[cow|cow]] and [[chicken|chicken]] competition offers the player a chance to make their [[farm-animal|farm animal]]s produce if they win. There is also a pet race, where the performance of the pet relies on their relationship with the owner. The booth sells animal themed items.
After approaching a festival orb, the player will spawn in front of their house at 21:00.
Beach Cleanup Day - Day 27

This festival takes place in the [[beach|beach]], starting between 9:00 - 14:00. There is also a shop that sells items and optional games. The tug of war and swimming competition relies heavily on the player's [[energy|stamina]]. The main event of the festival is a cutscene of the Townies' efforts to clean up the beach. To initiate the main event, interact with the main event monument centrally located on the beach.
To end the festival, the player will need to go out from it's location. The player will then spawn in front of their house at 21:00.
Fall Festivals & Events
Harvest Festival - Day 15

This festival takes place at [[alun-alun-square|Alun-Alun Square]], East of the [[lake|Lake]], starting between 19:00 - 22:00. The Player can bring up to 6 items to compete against [[bobby|Bobby]], a farmer from Beluga Bay, in the harvest competition. This competition is judged by [[jeff-smith|Jeff Smith]]. Players can also take part in an apple bobbing minigame, located in the south of the festival, and a pumpkin smashing minigame, located in the south-east of the festival. There is also a possibility of buying certain rare items from the Harvest Festival Shop, located in the north of the festival. [[pufferfish-drilling-corp|Pufferfish]] also has a booth in the north of the festival, but there is currently nothing for sale from this booth.
Spooky Day Festival - Day 28

This festival takes place in the [[starlet-town|Starlet Town]] center, starting between 19:00 - 22:00. There are 2 carnival mini games that can be played multiple times. The scavenger hunt requires the player to find 5 purple eyeballs scattered around the festival grounds. They can redeem their prize at the chest by the fountain. The shop sells halloween themed items and decor, including two exclusive [[scarecrow|scarecrow]] recipes from buying the scarecrows. The main activity is an Ogoh ogoh parade.
Winter Festivals & Events
Winter Festival - Day 17 - 21

The Winter Festival or Winter Fair is the first and longest festival of Winter. It starts at 5pm and takes place at the [[beach|Beach]] on the lower side of Starlet Town. This festival is the only one that doesn't have a festival orb, and the in-game time will not stop. The festival booths sell a wide variety of [[clothing|clothing]], [[consumables|food]], [[furniture|furniture]] and other items. There are trivia and 4 mini games, including one where the player comes head to head with [[bobby|Bobby]] again in a match pattern game. There is no main event, and rewards can only be won once per festival.
New Year Eve Feast - Day 28

This festival takes place at the [[hillside-brewery-and-vineyard|vineyard]] between 19:00 - 22:00. The main event is a fireworks display over the [[hot-spring|hot springs]], which can be started by interacting with the festival orb located in the center of the vineyard. The Player can participate in a Don't Drop Balloon minigame, located beside the [[observatory|Observatory]]. The Player can also spin the lucky wheel to receive a random gift.

crafting.x: Crafting is a game mechanic in Coral Island that allows the player to create items according to the crafting recipes. The items can be used for [[farming|farming]], processing raw materials into [[artisan-product|artisan products]] and other resources, decorating the player's [[farm|farm]], and other purposes. The player knows seven crafting recipes at the start of the game, and must learn all others by gaining masteries level, doing some quests or purchase them. All crafted items will be base quality regardless the quality of ingredients used.
Menu

The Crafting menu can be accessed by pressing the "T" button or by opening any menu and navigating to the hammer and axe symbol. The menu shows all recipes the player currently knows. In order to craft an item, the player has to have all its necessary ingredients in their [[inventory|inventory]] or stored in global chest. Items from left to right, top to bottom will be prioritized as ingredients, and items in inventory will be prioritized over global chest as well. The recipes the player is able to craft will be filled in, while recipes with missing ingredients are faded out.
The player can view an item's description and the materials required to craft it by hovering the cursor over the item.

To craft an item, the player needs to click on the item's icon once they have all the required ingredients. The newly crafted item will appear in the first empty inventory slot. All items are crafted instantly.
List of crafted items
Storage
The player can craft chests to store their items in.
Farming

Resource equipment
These items are used to process raw resources into more valuable ones.
Item producers
These items produce new items once placed, either automatically or by duplicating an input item.
Decor
The player can craft signs, gates, fences, and paths to decorate their farm.
Badges

merfolk.x: The Merfolk reside in the [[merfolk-kingdom|Merfolk Kingdom]] under the sea. There are many merfolk villages around the world, but there is one located by the coast of Coral Island.

Submerged artifacts suggest that the Merfolk Kingdom protected the oceans. It appears they were tasked with ruling the underwater world around Coral Island, making sure that order was maintained. Once upon a time, they worked with the [[giant|Giants]] and the [[goddess-of-flowers|Goddess of Flowers]] to maintain the island's balance.
The Merfolk have their own language, Merakih, that will need to be deciphered to understand and speak with them and to built your relationships with them.

Due to land-dwellers past and current actions (i.e. trash littering the sea floor and the oil roots slowly killing the Coral Tree), some merfolk have adopted cautious and isolationist views. Others are curious and fascinated by land-dwellers.

The player first encounters [[agung|Agung]] and [[denali|Denali]] while [[diving|diving]]. Development updates have revealed [[miranjani|Princess Miranjani]] and [[semeru|Semeru]] the leader of the guard, as well as the silhouettes of several others.
Three of the Merfolk will be [[romance|romance]]able when the game is fully released: Denali, Miranjani and Semeru.

giant.x: Legend has it that the Kingdom of Giants existed to cultivate the rich soil of Coral Island. Ruins around the island depict Giants and what appear to be humans farming alongside one another.
In the past, Giants worked alongside the [[goddess-of-flowers|Goddess of Flowers]] and the [[merfolk|Merfolk]] to maintain the balance of the island.
Despite their species' name, the giants are actually very short.

The types of enchantments available depend on the type of tool it is being applied to. The quality/level of the enchantment and the number of enchantments that can be applied depend on the number giants freed and the quality level of the tool respectively.
The Enchantment Shrine can be found in the center of the [[giant-village|Giant's Village]]

Levels correspond to how many giants have been freed. For example, 2 giants freed means the tool can be upgraded to level 2. Note: The bug net and fishing pole have possible enchantments listed, but have no enchantment slots.

enchanting.x: There are two modes of enchantment: adding or upgrading. The cost for adding enchantment is always 100. Adding has the chance to obtain the same enchantment which will automatically upgrade the particular enchantment. Adding can always be performed. Upgrading on the other hand is more targeted to specific enchantment, and the cost will grow up along the level of the enchantment. Upgrading can't be performed if there is no other enchantment that can be upgraded.

Only up to 5 items can be used as points per adding/upgrading enchantments. Adding or upgrading can only be done if the point(s) requirement is met. Any extras of points will be used for the next adding/upgrading.

The points used to pay for enchantments are acquired by offering gems, fossils, and artifacts. The number of points awarded for an object depends on the item's rarity, with rarer items being worth more points than more common ones.

fossil.x: Fossils are the valuable bones of ancient creatures that can be found by processing fossil nodes at the [[laboratory|Laboratory]]. Fossils can be donated to the [[museum|Museum]] to complete the collection, sold for money, or used for [[enchanting|enchanting]] or gifts.
In addition to being found in fossil nodes, most fossils can also be purchased at the [[black-market|Black Market]] for an increased price.

Each fossil can be donated to the museum once for 3 points Museum. Completing donation for all 60 fossils will also earn 40 points Museum as well as unique reward from museum and succès « Paleontologist ». Fossils can be duplicated through [[slime-of-replication|slime of replication]] and can also be sold or [[gift|gift]]ed; however, they are considered universally hated gifts.

As of v0.3, fossils can also be used as fuel for the enchanting system with certain fossils being worth a set amount of points based on their rarity. A list of all items that can be used for enchanting and their point values can be found on the [[enchanting|Enchanting]] page.
4 fossils of any type are needed for the Master Slime section of the [[guardian-mural|Guardian Mural]] altar.

Fossil nodes can only be obtained after obtaining [[soft-bristle-brush|Soft Bristle Brush]]. The nodes can be obtained by tilling sand or soil with a [[hoe|hoe]], clearing trash with a [[scythe|scythe]] while [[diving|diving]], or breaking rocks around the island, underwater or in the [[cavern|cavern]] with a [[pickaxe|pickaxe]]. Identifying the contents of a fossil node costs 20 per piece at the Laboratory.

calendar.x: The calendar, located in the [[community-center|Community Center]], depicts the events that occur during the 28-day [[calendar|seasons]] in Coral Island. These events include [[festival|festivals]] and [[townies|townies]]' birthdays; the [[player|player character]]'s birthday cannot be set in-game.

There are four seasons per year: [[spring|Spring]], [[summer|Summer]], [[fall|Fall]], and [[winter|Winter]]. Follow the floating glowing flower petals to the left side of your farm and continue the path until you see a way (big tree trunk used as the bridge) that would lead to the creature's home.

There, a cutscene will play where you will talk to the "Chieftain" and you will be granted the "Third Eye" which gives you the ability to read and understand the language of old. The tablets on the shrines will now be readable.
