There's a lot to explore in Coral Island, including:

i: [[starlet-town|Starlet Town]] is the heart of Coral Island. Not only is it roomy and features a butterfly garden, but this charming little town also has stories hidden behind its townies.
The [[beach|Beach]] is rich with sparkly white sands, seashells, and seasonal fruits. On the pier sits a handsome old [[coral-inn|Inn]] and a gateway to ocean exploration, the [[diving|Diving]] spot.

The [[lake|Lake]] guards perhaps the most magical place in Coral Island. Find your way through the wooden bridge and discover the ancient temple. It’s believed to be the main source of water and where the island's rich soil originates from.
The [[forest|Forest]] is a mystic sanctuary for wildlife, filled with ruins and who-knows-what. Underneath the musky floor, it's a hoarding place for messages from the past, the [[cavern|Cavern]].

The [[lookout|Lookout]] used to be a place where locals prepared for battles of old and whatnot. As time passed, the [[lighthouse|Lighthouse]] is now solely used for navigational aid. Come here and enjoy wicked sunsets and pick some wild fruits on your way home.

The [[woodlands|Woodlands]] used to be part of the Forest, but since the arrival of humans, it is now tamed and family-friendly, without losing its green allure. Walk alongside the river to see the [[starlet-elementary-school|School]], [[emmas-taco-truck|Taco Truck]], and houses belonging to those who prefer quiet nights over paved pathways of the town.
[[hillside|Hillside]], sandwiched between the Forest and Woodlands, is the perfect combination of green and privacy. Take a peek at the Vineyard and familiarize yourself with the local Carpenters.

romance.x: All of the romanceable characters have several variant outfits that change depending on [[calendar|season]] and event: one standard outfit per season, one bathing suit outfit, and one festival outfit. By contrast, non-romanceable characters have one standard outfit per season, for a total of over 170 unique outfits between all of the NPCs in Coral Island.
Romance candidates

Out of the 50+ characters living on the island, 30 characters are romanceable. Though [[ben|Ben]], [[charles|Charles]], [[millie|Millie]], and [[suki|Suki]] were not initially romance candidates, they were added to the original 16-character roster after Coral Island's Kickstarter crowdfunding campaign reached its US$750,000 stretch goal. With the release of version 1.0, three additional romanceable characters were introduced: Miranjani, Semeru, and Denali, all of whom are merfolk. The version 1.3 update, "Ocean and Kisses", added two more romanceable characters: Agung and Raina.
It is also possible to marry another player in multiplayer mode. Multiplayer is not confirmed to be cross-platform but is under consideration for later in development.

Once the player has reached level 8 of [[friendship|friendship]], they will receive a letter from [[sanchez-brothers-blacksmith|Sanchez Brothers Blacksmith]], telling them that to show romantic interest the player must give them a [[locket|locket]] that is newly added into their catalog. The locket costs 1,500 or.

The player can date as many marriage candidates as they want at once. However, the player can only marry one person. Also, if Jealousy has not been disabled, dating multiple characters can trigger a breakup event.
If the player does not give a person a locket, their friendship level maximum will be capped at 8 hearts, and any heart events above 8 hearts will be unavailable to the player.

If the player rejected the romance candidate at their 10th heart event, their heart would decay by 2 levels. Furthermore they will refuse to talk with player for 3 days. However, the dating status would still be maintained. When the player wants to propose to the marriage candidate (after reaching level 10 of friendship), they will need to buy a [[diamond-ring|diamond ring]] at the [[sanchez-brothers-blacksmith|blacksmith]]. The proposal ring costs 5,000 or then gift it to them. Gifting diamond ring does not count toward weekly gifting limit.
Proposal prerequisite
For a successful proposal, the player needs to complete the following requirements:

romance.x: After those requirements have been met, the player can give a diamond ring to the marriage candidate. Any proposal attempts before fulfilling all requirements will be rejected. After a successful proposal, the wedding ceremony will take place three days after the proposal date. For example, if the player proposes on Spring 3, the wedding will be held on Spring 6.

If the player wants to wear [[white-flamingo|wedding clothes]] during the ceremony, it should be purchased in advance and put on before leaving the house on the wedding day. Each spouse has their own unique wedding clothes.
Post wedding

After the wedding, the spouse of the player will move into the player's farmhouse, they will occupy the center room of the second floor. Each spouse has a unique room designs that reflects their character, these room has a set layout and cannot be customized or decorated by the player. If the player's spouse is a [[merfolk|Merfolk]], they will go back to [[merfolk-kingdom|Merfolk Kingdom]] once per season and spend one night there.

After marriage, the spouse's maximum heart level increases to 15, and the weekly gift limit is removed. At the start of each day, there is a chance that the spouse will give the player a gift. The spouse may randomly ask the player for a hug, kiss, or a hangout when you interact with them.
Each night, there is a random chance for a Woohoo event to occur. This feature can be enabled or disabled in the game settings.
Previously, the player able to give a locket and date someone after getting married. However, as the latest update you can't do so anymore.
Children

As per current version, player can have some interaction with the children. If the player marries [[suki|Suki]], [[valentina|Valentina]] will move into Suki's room so as not to reduce the number of new children the player can have.

in order to be able have a child, player must fulfill the requirements of having [[farmhouse|farmhouse]] upgrade level 4, which unlock the left and right room on the second floor. This room serves as the children's room, they have fixed layout and cannot be customized or decorated by the player.

After getting married, each morning there will be a chance for the spouse to ask whether the player wants to have a child. This chance is based on the spouse's heart level; The higher the heart level, the greater the chance of the event occuring. After player acceptance, it takes 14 days for the children to arrive. kickstarter-campaign.x: Coral Island was partially funded through a successful Kickstarter campaign, a crowdfunding effort Stairway Games began to expand on the available content within the game. Pledges can no longer be made, altered, or cancelled via Kickstarter since the campaign has concluded, but existing pledges can be edited for add-ons via BackerKit. For those unable to contribute to the Kickstarter, Stairway Games is in the process of creating a pre-order option.

The campaign was live from February 1, 2021 through March 3, 2021, with USD currency for all goals and backer pledges, and met the initial funding goal of $70,000 within 36 hours of the campaign launch. Following initial funding, further expansions to the original game were introduced through funding stretch goals. A total of $1,639,368 was raised by 36,374 backers over the 30-day period; additional statistics regarding the amount funded or pledges made per day can be found on Kicktraq, a website unaffiliated with Kickstarter, Inc.
Several in-game perks are exclusive to Kickstarter backers, including exclusive clothing and [[pet|pets]].

The first group of stretch goals were introduced on February 2, 2021, going up to $600,000. When the first set of goals was successfully funded halfway through the Kickstarter on February 15, 2021, Stairway Games released a second set of stretch goals up to $1,250,000. On February 26, 2021, the Kickstarter met the final stretch goal with the help of over 27,000 backers and declared that all additional funds would be reinvested into polishing the game.

cooking.x: Cooking is a game mechanic in Coral Island that allows the player to cook a variety of [[consumables|consumable]] items. These items can be eaten by the player, sold, or given as [[gift|gift]]s to other characters.

Cooking becomes available after the player upgrades their [[farmhouse|farmhouse]] with a kitchen. The player can use the recipes they have learned to turn simple ingredients into dishes or attempt to cook them manually.

If the player has obtained the recipe for a dish as well as the necessary utensils and ingredients, the dish can be prepared automatically by the selecting the recipe from the cooking menu. Ingredients can be brought in inventory or stored in global chest.

Some of the recipes can be obtained mainly from reaching certain [[friendship|heart level]] with certain characters. If the recipe hasn't been learned, a dish can still be prepared by manually selecting the correct utensils and ingredients in the cooking menu and completing a brief mini-game. Successfully cooking manually will learn the recipe if it's not been learned.

Once the ingredients and utensils are selected and the dish started, a bar with a slider and a highlighted section will appear on the screen. The player is required to click or interact when the slider is in the highlighted area to successfully complete the dish.

Any combination of incorrect ingredients or utensils or failure of the mini-game when manually cooking will result in a [[failed-dish|failed dish]]. Currently only base quality of failed dish will be obtained regardless the quality of ingredients used.

Cooking ingredients can be obtained in a variety of ways: by [[farming|farming]], [[foraging|scavenging]], or [[fishing|fishing]]. Some dishes require the player to use the exact ingredient, others require an ingredient from a certain group of ingredients (e.g., [[egg-group|any egg]], [[vegetable-group|any vegetable]], or [[fish-group|any fish]]). Some of these groups match the in-game groups used for [[artisan-product|artisan products]] and [[friendship|gifting]], other are detailed below. Black honey does not count as honey for cooking.
The quality of ingredients used affects the quality of the dish. Higher quality dish affects the selling price and longer duration of the buff.

catching.x: Catching is one of many activities available on Coral Island. Over 30 kinds of [[insect|insect]]s and [[sea-critter|critter]]s can be captured with [[bug-net|bug net]], documented, and donated to the [[museum|museum]]. This past-time was added to the game due to the [[kickstarter-campaign|Kickstarter campaign]] successfully meeting one of its early stretch goals.
Catching mastery

The Catching mastery pertains to all things having to do with catching [[insect|insects]] and [[sea-critter|ocean critters]] in the wild. The catching proficiency is increased as the player gain level in their catching mastery. Gaining levels also allows them to obtain new [[crafting|crafting]] recipes or points to spend for new skill.
Experience

The player can increase their catching mastery level by regularly spending their time catching insects and ocean critters. The more difficult an insect or critter is to catch, the more mastery experience it brings, with a bonus for the quality of the creature caught. Catching insects/critters using traps will also provide points and trigger skill if learned. Breeding insects through [[insect-house|insect house]] is also a good way to earn points even though lack of triggering learned skills.

catching.x: Levels
Reaching a new level in catching mastery grants the player new [[crafting|crafting]] recipes when they go to sleep to end their day.
Skills

Every other level of catching mastery gained allows the player to unlock one skill. The player will be able to unlock up to five skills by leveling up. The last skill can be unlocked by purchasing [[merit-points|catching elixir]].

catching.x: Proficiency

The higher the player's catching level is, the less energy it costs to use [[bug-net|bug net]]. Using [[consumables|consumables]] that grant a [[buff|catching proficiency buff]] can temporarily further reduce the stamina cost.
Using bug net

Bug net can be obtained as early as on day 3 of the first year by completing « Visit the Beach Shack », and can be further upgraded. The upgraded nets cost the same amount of [[energy|energy]] to use but have increased catch angle and radius compared to the basic net.

To catch an insect or a critter, the player needs to approach it in the wild and swing their bug net using the left mouse button, aiming it so the insect is inside the net's catch area and is highlighted. If the player releases the button when the insect is highlighted, the insect is transferred to their [[inventory|inventory]].

All insects and critters will notice the player approaching, as shown with a circle alertness indicator above them. If the player fails to catch the creature before its circle indicator fills completely, the creature rapidly flees; it can still be caught while fleeing. The harder an insect or a creature are to catch, the faster it moves, the more easily it is alerted to the player's presence, and the faster its circle indicator fills.
All bug nets cost 20 energy to use if the player catches an insect or a critter or 1 energy if the swing fails.
Using traps

There are 4 types of catching traps in total. Traps can be placed on the ground on the land to attract [[insect|insects]] or in the ocean to attract [[sea-critter|critters]], and for each there are different traps to catch floating/flying catchable or crawling catchable.
Using scents
There are also 4 types of scents scents that can be used by consuming them or can be placed on the corresponding traps.

trinket.x: Trinkets are items that the player can equip to provide various effects, such as boosting stats or giving off light. The player can have two trinkets equipped at once.
Trinkets can be equipped or unequipped using the trinket slots at the bottom the inventory.

storage.x: There are different type of storage in Coral Island.

Chest is a type of storage that can hold most types of items. The current best chest has a capacity of 40 storage slots. Chest can be set to be a global chest. Items inside global chest can be used for crafting and cooking.
Fridge is a unique non-movable chest that come with the house lv 2.

House (storage) is a unique storage that can hold furniture. It has a capacity of 999 storage slots. Any [[furniture|furniture]] removed during decor mode will automatically be put in house (storage).
Sprinkler attachment is a type of storage that can hold seeds, [[fertilizer|fertilizers]] or [[crop|crops]].
Wardrobe is a type of storage that can hold clothing. Different wardrobes access the same storage.

bait.x: Bait is an item that can be placed in inventory to influence the fish caught.
The player will learn to [[crafting|craft]] baits as they level their [[fishing|Fishing]] mastery.

All baits are used by placing them in an empty slot on equipment inside the inventory. It also can be used on any [[fish-trap|fish trap]] to help it catch fish. The baits will be used by 1 every time player catches something from [[fishing-pole|fishing pole]].

coral-coin.x: Coral coins are the primary form of currency used on Coral Island. The amount of coins the player has on them is displayed on the upper right corner of the screen below the in-game [[calendar|date]] and [[game-time|time]].

Coins are generally accumulated through collecting and selling items obtained by [[farming|farming]], [[ranching|ranching]], [[foraging|foraging]], [[mining|mining]], [[diving|diving]], [[catching|catching]], [[fishing|fishing]], and [[combat|combat]]. Said items can be sold using the shipping bin on the player's farm or directly to shops in or around town. There is no difference in income between selling to a shop or through the shipping bin, though shops will frequently only buy certain items and the shipping bin only pays out at the end of the day, after the player has gone to sleep.
Coins can also be obtained as rewards for completing [[quest|quests]] or by playing mini-games at [[festival|festival]]s.
Earning certain number of coins will earn certain [[badges|badges]].

insect-trap.x: An insect trap is a [[tool|tool]] used to catch [[insect|insect]]s around the island.
The player will learn to [[crafting|craft]] insect traps as they level their [[catching|Catching]] mastery.

All insect traps are used by placing them in an empty 1x1 space in an outdoor area of the island, such as in the town, in the forest, or on the beach. It cannot be placed on the farm, in the cavern, underwater, or in any indoor space.

Once placed, insect trap can passively catch nearby insects or have a chance of one spawning inside of it overnight. Using a corresponding insect scent guarantees an insect spawning overnight. The insects that can be caught are based on the insects that can naturally be found in the area where the trap is placed, and are more likely to catch ground-based or flying insects depending on the type of trap and scent used.
Insect traps may be destroyed after the player leaves a [[festival|festival]].
The traps can also be enhanced by the corresponding scents.

critter-trap.x: A crawler trap is a [[tool|tool]] used to catch [[sea-critter|critter]]s in the ocean.
The player will learn to [[crafting|craft]] crawler traps as they level their [[catching|Catching]] mastery.
All crawler traps are used by placing them in an empty 1x1 space in any outdoor space while diving. It cannot be placed in underwater caves, or in any indoor space.

Once placed, a crawler trap can passively catch nearby critters or have a chance of one spawning inside of it overnight. Using a corresponding crawler scent guarantees a critter spawning overnight. The critters that can be caught are based on the critters that can naturally be found in the area where the trap is placed, and are more likely to catch crawling or floating critters depending on the type of trap and scent used.
The traps can also be enhanced by the corresponding scents.
